quest.title: A Commission Catches You in Natlan
quest.description: You and Paimon bump into a squad of Fatui at the Masters of the Night-Wind, and you meet their employer. Thus does a commission from Fontaine find its way to you...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x350, Mora x31125, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

chapter.num: Memories Flowing With Color: Act III
chapter.title: The Truth of the Battle of Seven Colors

talks.objective: Go to the Masters of the Night-Wind

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What are the Fatui doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's a little concerning... Let's go over there and see what they're up to.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Also, how did they get this close to a tribal settlement?

choices.text: Well, considering what The Captain did for Natlan...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh... All the Fatui left in Natlan are probably The Captain's subordinates. That basically makes them followers of one of Natlan's heroes.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Still, once a Fatuus always a Fatuus. Something seems off, seeing them here... Let's go check it out!

choices.text: Maybe they've been given a bit more leeway.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ahem! What are you guys doing here?
Heh, following orders. If you have a problem, take it up with our employer.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, what's with the attitude? Can the Fatui even work for a private employer?
Ahem! This is Grudoc — I hired him to be my bodyguard in Natlan. As you can see, he's not the sociable type. I'm sorry for any offense.
My original plan was to hire someone from the local tribes, but a priest recommended Grudoc and his squad.
I was told they were capable fighters and had the time to spare, so they fit the bill... It seems like the Fatui's reputation in Natlan is quite positive.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, that's what happened... Then, you must be from Fontaine?

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: #Precisely! Montluson, at your service. I work in the publication business. And you two... Wait, you must be {NICKNAME} and {M#his}{F#her} fairy companion!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, you know us?

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: A golden-haired Traveler with a floating companion... There's no mistake!

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: Your exploits in Fontaine have all the makings of a best-selling series! I'd be a failure of a book merchant if I couldn't recognize you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Wow, we're really famous at this point, {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: It's truly my lucky day! I know this is sudden, but I was actually looking for you two... You see, I have a favor to ask.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, you... chased us all the way to Natlan? That's a little creepy...

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: You'll be generously rewarded, I promise you!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Well, at least he got straight to the point. Should we hear what he has to say?

choices.text: Something tells me we can't escape this one.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *ahem*... Alright, we'll hear your request.

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: You know the great shaman, Citlali, right? I need her help with something!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... Yeah, but the chances of her helping a random stranger just because we asked...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: With her personality? Pretty slim...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, Citlali really doesn't like dealing with strangers...

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: I heard about that from other members of her tribe. But, they told me if one person could convince her, it would be the golden-haired Traveler.

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: If you manage it, I'll even double your pay!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Why do you need her help?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, yeah... We should definitely get to the bottom of that first.

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: It's kind of a long story, and there's tribal history involved, so you should hear it from an expert. Allier, if you could...

response.speaker: Allier
response.text: Of course! I don't often have an eager audience for this kind of thing... Nice to meet you. The name's Allier — I'm a Researcher from the Fontaine Research Institute.

response.speaker: Allier
response.text: Unlike most researchers, I have a keen interest in ancient ruins. That's why I was invited to join Monsieur Montluson's team.

response.speaker: Allier
response.text: Have you heard the legend of the great shaman, Huitzilin?

response.speaker: Allier
response.text: Yes. According to local records, she was a color mystic who lived over two hundred years ago, the most adept in her tribe at using that particular technique.

response.speaker: Allier
response.text: Out of all her exploits, her most celebrated is "the Battle of Seven Colors."

response.speaker: Allier
response.text: According to legend, the battle was triggered by an Abyss invasion, one of the most brutal in Natlan's history, even from a greater historical perspective.

response.speaker: Allier
response.text: Amazingly, Natlan was able to turn the tide despite being at an extreme disadvantage. The key to victory was none other than a "color" Huitzilin created on the battlefield.

response.speaker: Allier
response.text: The "color" was extraordinary — illusory in appearance while also seeming to possess physical form. Legend has it that Huitzilin used the "color" to construct a magnificent maze on the battlefield...

response.speaker: Allier
response.text: ...And trap all the enemies inside. This allowed her allies to launch a counterattack and, ultimately, secure victory.

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: *ahem*... Anyway, that's the gist of it. We don't want to take up too much of your time.

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: That story is the reason I came to Natlan. I often publish books about the history of other nations. They always end up faring well on the market.

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: When I heard this story for the first time, I wanted to include it in my next collection, but...

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: Historical records about Natlan aren't very detailed. We haven't been able to determine where the battle took place, or find any definitive evidence that it occurred at all.

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: Even within the Masters of the Night-Wind, people dispute the legitimacy of the story. Some believe it to be a myth.

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: If that were the case, the story would not be fit for publication...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, but, if you're just including it in a story collection, why does it matter if it never happened?

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: Well, you see, the slogan for the collection is "restoring the truth of history." Naturally, I need it to be factual.

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: That's why I'm here. The Masters of the Night-Wind are said to have a tradition of recording past events, so I wanted to consult their records.

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: But, I was refused access to the Obsidian Altar. Application after application, and all I received were a few ordinary woven scrolls with nothing to offer. Honestly, I'm just trying to promote their history, and they make such a fuss...

response.speaker: Allier
response.text: According to my research, their scrolls are considered sacred relics in addition to historical records. Naturally, outsiders are rarely granted access.

response.speaker: Allier
response.text: Not to mention, the scrolls we did get to review actually contain a huge amount of information. I just need more time, and I could—

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: We've been over this, Allier. There's no need to waste time on those scrolls when we have a better way.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Citlali, you mean?

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: Exactly. You're well aware, I'm sure, that Citlali has been alive for more than two hundred years. That means she lived during the era of the Battle of Seven Colors!

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: If she agrees to be my consultant, then no other historical records are necessary.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, that's what you want...

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: So, what do you say? I'll quadruple the pay if it helps sweeten the deal!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, it's not that we don't want to help you...

choices.text: We actually should go ask her, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, right! The duty the chief gave us has a lot to do with Huitzilin...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Who knows? The "Battle of Seven Colors" might lead us in the right direction!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, we'll help you convince Citlali. Just let us do the talking, okay?

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: Of course!

choices.text: We still have a duty to fulfill, after all.
She's the one that worked with colors, right?
And if the pay is good...

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: So, this is where the great shaman lives? A bit... far from civilization, isn't it? I hope the person who pointed us in this direction wasn't mistaken...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: For someone like Citlali, it actually makes a lot of sense.

dialogues.speaker: Allier
dialogues.text: Is this graffiti her work, too? I wonder if it's a cultural practice... If I could just copy it down—

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: We're here for a reason, Allier. As agreed, you two can do the talking, and we'll wait for you here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, we'll go knock on the door! Hopefully she's not hungover...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Citlali? Are you there? We need your help with something!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...No response. Maybe she's not home?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's try her other name.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, uh... Granny Itztli? Are you home?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The door is thrown open, and you're met with the pungent smell of alcohol.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Hey, kid! If you're here to challenge me, book an appointment first!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (So, Citlali's a real hermit, huh...)

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: #...{NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The door closes abruptly.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Looks like we came at a bad time.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: *ahem*! Are you still there? Just come in, we can talk inside.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, at least we didn't get turned away...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, so this is where Citlali lives...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I, uh, didn't have time to fully clean up the place... Complain if you want. Menial housework means nothing to a great shaman like myself.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Besides, in light novels, people who keep everything neat and tidy are always too boring to be the protagonists.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Also, I'm not a hermit. I'm just above superficial rules of societal etiquette.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She sure does care a lot about what we think of her...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Oh, and that spell I used to transfer my senses to you... You're not still, uh, experiencing the side-effects, are you?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: It's my duty as a great shaman to check that kind of thing.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, you mean when we could hear your thoughts? Nope! It's been so long. We don't have to worry about that anymore, right?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: #Then, why do I hear {NICKNAME}'s thoughts in my head?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Oh, she heard me call her a hermit... That bothers her? I thought she was "above superficial rules of societal etiquette"...)

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I can still hear you, y'know!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I apologize for offending you...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Don't bother, I'll find a way to fix it. First you hear my thoughts, now I'm hearing your thoughts...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: It was just a simple spell. I use it on you, and now it's on the fritz...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Forget it. Just tell me why you're here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, someone asked us... to ask you... to be their consultant. They have questions about the history of Natlan.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: So, they asked the hero of Natlan to put in a good word? Sounds like they know I don't usually trouble myself with other people's problems.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The pay is really good!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Doesn't matter. I'm busy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She sure doesn't look busy... Paimon knew this wouldn't get us anywhere...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What if the request comes from me?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: From you...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, we were given a sacred duty to help your tribe weave a special scroll!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Huh? So, you're the appointed ones this time?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We were surprised, too! After all, we have no idea how to weave a scroll like that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But, with Chief Biram's help, we were able to make some progress!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We still haven't succeeded, but we learned that the key to weaving the scroll is a special kind of color.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The historical event those men want to ask about also involves color. If you help them, you might end up helping us, too!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She's giving us that face again... Did Paimon not explain things clearly?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I can't decide whether this twist is completely out of the blue, or if it was foreshadowed all along...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um... Does that mean you won't help us?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I... I need to think about it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then, there's still hope!

dialogues.speaker: Grudoc
dialogues.text: Hey! What's the hold-up? Just give us an answer already!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Y—You agreed to let us do the talking!

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Ugh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Citlali...

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: Stand down, Grudoc! As your employer, if I tell you to wait, then you wait.

dialogues.speaker: Grudoc
dialogues.text: Understood.

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: You're the great shaman who's been alive for centuries? But you're so... Ahem, apologies for the disturbance. Grudoc is a recent hire — so difficult to restrain sometimes.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew... You're lucky you didn't force Citlali's hand.

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: Well, since you're here, how about a discussion...?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Do you have any idea who I am? Did you think Granny Itztli would be fooled by your little performance?

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: Um...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I have no intention of speaking to you. Your "recent hire" interrupted me right as I was about to make an important decision.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Pull a trick like that again, and I'll make your lives a living horror novel, except ten times worse. That's all I came out here to say.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, we have a discussion to finish.

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: You live up to your name, Granny Itztli. I apologize for the offence. I'm just surprised the Battle of Seven Colors didn't pique your interest...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: You're investigating the Battle of Seven Colors?

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: #Ah, {NICKNAME} didn't get to that part?

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: #Yes, I thought {NICKNAME} could help me convince you. But, if I'm not mistaken, you have a personal interest in this matter, don't you?

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: I heard that the great shaman, Huitzilin, was a friend of yours. You two must have been close...

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: If I can resolve the controversy and prove the Battle took place, I'll include it in my next collection. Then, all of Teyvat will learn the truth.

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: With your support, your friend's heroic deeds will once again be known throughout the land... Inspiring, don't you think?

choices.text: You'll be helping me fulfill my duty.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: If this is really about that duty, then... Fine, I'll help you.

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: I'm honored—

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: #Save it — I agreed to help {NICKNAME}, not you. You'll just have to leech what you can.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, at least she agreed to help...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Looks like my friendship with Citlali came in handy after all. I never took her to be the heartless type, anyway.)

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Who are you calling heartless?

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: #Not a problem! I always planned to work with {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: So, did you directly experience any events of the Battle? Do you have any idea where it took place? Can you think of any relics we could use to prove it?

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Talk at me why don't you...

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: Um...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'd like to know, too.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: Fine — no, no, and no.

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: Uh...

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: I did live during the same era as her, but that doesn't mean we experienced the same events. I've lived a long time, but I'm not a walking encyclopedia.

response.speaker: Citlali
response.text: You decide the angle of your investigation, and I'll provide answers if I'm familiar with the subject.

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: ...Alright. Even if you didn't witness the battle yourself, you still lived through that era. Your insights are very valuable!

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: Allier, you had an idea about where to start, yes?

response.speaker: Allier
response.text: Oh, well, my plan was to consult the members of the tribe in charge of recording history.

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: Then, let's start there.

response.speaker: Montluson
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, what do you say to officially working together? After all, it appears I can only get Miss Citlali's help through you.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sounds good.

choices.text: And it would mean a lot to your tribe.

dialogues.speaker: Allier
dialogues.text: A great shaman who has lived for hundreds of years... If she agrees to help us, there are so many things we could research!

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: Allier, as the provider of your research funding, I suggest you focus on our current mission. It's very important to me.

dialogues.speaker: Allier
dialogues.text: Sorry. Maybe, if we get a chance in the future, then...

dialogues.speaker: Montluson
dialogues.text: We'll cross that bridge when we come to it.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Citlali suddenly walks out, and you rush after her.
